facts.statement: Huanhepterus lived during the Early Cretaceous period in what is now Qingyang, Gansu, China.
facts.quote: Huanhepterus is an extinct genus of ctenochasmatid pterodactyloid pterosaur from the Early Cretaceous period of what is now Qingyang, Gansu, China.

facts.statement: The genus Huanhepterus was named by Dong Zhiming in 1982.
facts.quote: The genus was named by Dong Zhiming in 1982.

facts.statement: The fossil was found in May 1978 in a quarry operated by the Sanshilipu commune after an explosion exposed a vertebra.
facts.quote: The fossil was in May 1978 found in a quarry operated by the Sanshilipu-commune, when an explosion exposed a vertebra.

facts.statement: The force of the explosion that exposed the fossil obliterated the right half of the specimen.
facts.quote: Its force obliterated the right half of the specimen.

facts.statement: Huanhepterus had about 26 pairs of slender teeth in the upper jaw and 25 in the lower, which became shorter away from the 11th pair and were absent in the posterior part of the snout.
facts.quote: The teeth, about 26 pairs in the upper and 25 in the lower jaws, were slender and numerous, and became shorter farther from the 11th pair, both to the front as to the back, where they become absent completely in posterior part of the snout.

facts.statement: Huanhepterus had long cervical vertebrae and toes, and lacked the fused complex of front dorsal vertebrae known as the notarium.
facts.quote: The cervical vertebrae were long, as were the toes, and there was no fused complex of the front dorsal vertebrae (notarium), as seen in other pterosaurs.

facts.statement: Huanhepterus is classified within the family Ctenochasmatidae and the subfamily Gnathosaurinae, in the basalmost position.
facts.quote: In the analysis, they recovered Huanhepterus within the family Ctenochasmatidae, more precisely within the subfamily Gnathosaurinae, though placed in the basalmost position.

facts.statement: Huanhepterus lived from the Valanginian to the Albian stages, between 137.05 and 100.5 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Valanginian to Albian (137.05 to 100.5 million years ago)
